message.content: The number of mitochondria in a cell varies widely depending on the cell type and its metabolic demands. In most mammalian cells, you’ll find somewhere between **100 and 500 mitochondria per cell**. Cells with high energy requirements—such as muscle cells, neurons, or sperm—can contain several thousand mitochondria, while cells with lower energy needs may have only a few dozen.
